title: Living Together
intro: In Class 4 EVS Chapter 1, Living Together, the topics are: Public Places in Our Community, helping hands in the community, van mahotsav: caring for nature, working together as a team, sharing a meal. Read the short notes, check every book question with the NCERT solutions, practise the important questions and then try the 30-mark sample paper. All four PDFs are free to download.
topics: Public Places in Our Community
A community is the people of a place and the places they share
Helping Hands in the Community
Every person in a community has a skill or an occupation
Van Mahotsav: Caring for Nature
Van Mahotsav, the Tree Planting Festival (1–7 July, rainy season), shows a community caring for nature and its shared places — ...
Working Together as a Team
When people form groups and each does one part of the job, big jobs become easy and problems get solved — at a festival, in times ...
Sharing a Meal
At a community feast everyone brings something, helps serve and eats together — sharing food and joy brings people closer

items: A community is the people of a place and the places they share. Public places — parks, schools, hospitals, roads, markets, bus stops — are used by everyone and connect people to each other.
People and places are part of our community.
Public places are shared by everyone.
Without them life would be hard — no place to learn, get treated, catch a bus or play.
Every person in a community has a skill or an occupation. When each person gives their skill, shared places get built and stay in good shape.
Each person helps with a skill.
Each job has its own tool: mason–trowel, carpenter–saw, gardener–watering can, electrician–pliers.

Van Mahotsav, the Tree Planting Festival (1–7 July, rainy season), shows a community caring for nature and its shared places — cleaning the park and planting trees so everyone gets better air and a greener earth.
Trees give better air and make the earth greener.
Van Mahotsav: 1–7 July, rainy season.
Care continues after the festival.
When people form groups and each does one part of the job, big jobs become easy and problems get solved — at a festival, in times of need and at school. Ants and bees live in teams too.
Divide the work — each one does a part.
Together, big jobs become quick and easy.
School is a team too.
At a community feast everyone brings something, helps serve and eats together — sharing food and joy brings people closer. Even the leaf plates are shared back with the soil as manure.
Everyone brings, serves and eats together.
Sharing builds bonds and happy memories.
Wrong: A public place belongs to nobody, so nobody needs to look after it. Right: It belongs to everyone, so everyone must keep it clean and safe
Wrong: Only people with big jobs help the community. Right: Every job matters — the sweeper, the mason and the gardener all keep the park going
Wrong: Once a sapling is planted, our job is over. Right: Saplings need watering and care — the children decided to look after the park every day
Wrong: In a team everyone does the same job. Right: Each member has a special job — like ants that collect food, look after babies or guard the home
Wrong: Sharing means only giving away things you don't need. Right: The villagers shared their own vegetables, cereals, work and fun

sol_items: Why do we need parks, schools, hospitals and bus stops ...: We learn, get treated, travel and play there; they help everyone.
What can you do to keep these places clean and saf: Do not litter, use dustbins and report damage.
Identify people who help maintain your locality and the...: Sweeper, gardener, electrician, mason, shopkeeper.
List the work, materials, tools and skills needed to de...: Mason with trowel, gardener with watering can, carpenter with saw, electrician with pliers.
Is it important for communities to come together in tim...: Yes, because together big problems become easy to solve.
Ways to take care of nature and our neighbourhood: Plant and water trees, keep parks clean and avoid littering.
imp_items: What is a community?
The people of a place together with the places they share
Name two public places and say why they matter.
A park and a hospital; everyone uses them
Why must everyone keep public places clean?
They belong to everyone
Who uses a trowel?
A mason
The street light is broken. Whom do we call?
An electrician
Match four jobs with their tools.
Mason: trowel; carpenter: saw; gardener: watering can; electrician: pliers

subject: EVS
title: Exploring Our Neighbourhood
intro: In Class 4 EVS Chapter 2, Exploring Our Neighbourhood, the topics are: Public Places, post office, bus stop, metro and flyover, hospital / health centre, bank, saving money, communication, finding our way. Read the short notes, check every book question with the NCERT solutions, practise the important questions and then try the 30-mark sample paper. All four PDFs are free to download.
topics: Public Places
Public places are places in our neighbourhood that give services to everyone — for health, safety, cleanliness or the environment
Post Office
A post office helps people stay connected: a letter dropped in a postbox is collected by the postman, sorted by region at the ...
Bus Stop, Metro and Flyover
Buses, metro trains and flyovers help people travel; metro and flyovers save travellers' time
Hospital / Health Centre
A hospital is an important part of the community: people come when unwell, and many people work there as a team
Bank
A bank keeps our money safe and helps us save for the future
Saving Money
Saving means keeping some money aside for future needs — in a piggy bank or a bank
Communication
The ways people communicate have changed: drumbeats and rock carvings → messengers and pigeons → postal service → telephone, ...
Finding Our Way
We find east from the rising sun and then the other directions

items: Public places are places in our neighbourhood that give services to everyone — for health, safety, cleanliness or the environment. Many people and vehicles work there to help the community.
Public places serve everyone.
They help with health, safety, cleanliness and the environment.
Many people and vehicles work there — we should thank them.

A post office helps people stay connected: a letter dropped in a postbox is collected by the postman, sorted by region at the post office and sent to its destination. Post offices also send parcels and important documents.
Postbox → postman → post office (sorting) → destination.
Post office helps people stay connected.
Buses, metro trains and flyovers help people travel; metro and flyovers save travellers' time. Development must be balanced with care for trees, birds and animals.
Flyovers take vehicles above busy crossings.
Metro trains are fast.
Development + planting trees = balance.
A hospital is an important part of the community: people come when unwell, and many people work there as a team. Hospitals also hold camps such as an Eye Check-up Camp.
People come to a hospital when they are unwell.
Many people with different roles work there.
Health camps help many people at once.

A bank keeps our money safe and helps us save for the future. An ATM lets us take out money anytime. Exchange changed from barter to money, and from Money Orders and bank queues to ATMs and sending money by phone.
Bank = money kept safe + savings.
ATM = take out money anytime.
Barter → money → Money Order → phone payment.
Saving means keeping some money aside for future needs — in a piggy bank or a bank. A budget plans how much to save and how much to spend.
Save first, then spend.
Savings + spending = total money.
Savings help with future needs.

The ways people communicate have changed: drumbeats and rock carvings → messengers and pigeons → postal service → telephone, radio, TV → mobile phones and internet. Communication is much faster now, but wrong news can spread fast too, so we check before sharing.
Communication evolved from drums to the internet.
Faster now — but check news before sharing.

We find east from the rising sun and then the other directions. On a map North is up, South is down, East is right and West is left. With directions and landmarks we can explain a route and draw a route map.
Sun rises in the east.
Map: N up, S down, E right, W left.
Directions + landmarks = clear route.
Wrong: Any place outside our home, like a friend's house, is a public place. Right: A public place gives a service to everyone; a friend's house belongs to one family
Wrong: The postman takes the letter straight from the postbox to the friend's house. Right: It first goes to the post office, where letters are sorted by region and sent on
Wrong: New flyovers and metros bring only good things. Right: They save time, but trees, birds and animals were lost — we must balance by planting trees
Wrong: Only the doctor works in a hospital. Right: Doctors, nurses, pharmacists, cleaners, drivers and others work as a team
Wrong: An ATM makes money or gives free money. Right: An ATM gives you your own money from your bank account
Wrong: Saving means never spending any money. Right: We spend on what we need and keep a part aside — that is a plan (budget)

sol_items: Write a letter to a friend and post it: Write the address, add a stamp and drop it in a postbox.
Field trip to a post office: what activities take place...: Sorting letters, selling stamps, sending parcels and documents.
How does the post office help people stay connecte: It carries letters, parcels and documents from place to place.
Interview elders on communication then and now: Then: letters, slow and few. Now: phones, fast and many.
Letters took long: how did it affect communication in t...: News took days or weeks; now we talk at once.
Wrong information spreads quickly: how can we make sure...: Check with a trusted source before sharing.
imp_items: What is a public place?
A place that gives services to everyone
Is a bus station a public place? Why?
Yes, it gives travel service to everyone
Why does the post office sort letters?
To send each letter towards its region quickly
Describe the journey of a letter.
Postbox, postman, post office sorting, destination
How does a flyover save time?
Vehicles go above busy crossings without stopping
Why must trees be planted when flyovers are built?
Trees, birds and animals are lost, so we balance development with care

title: Nature Trail
intro: In Class 4 EVS Chapter 3, Nature Trail, the topics are: Exploring a Nature Trail Safely, land animals and their features, birds — beaks, claws and food, animals in and around water, insects — tiny animals, leaves — colour, shape, texture and veins, web of life. Read the short notes, check every book question with the NCERT solutions, practise the important questions and then try the 30-mark sample paper. All four PDFs are free to download.
topics: Exploring a Nature Trail Safely
On a nature trail we explore plants and animals in their home; a nature scientist guides us, and we follow safety rules so that ...
Land Animals and Their Features
Many animals live on land in the forest
Birds — Beaks, Claws and Food
Birds differ in colour, eyesight, beaks and claws
Animals In and Around Water
Animals that live in and around water move in different ways and have special features to survive there — fins, webbed feet, ...
Insects — Tiny Animals
Insects are tiny animals with three pairs of legs and one pair of antennae to sense their surroundings; some, like flies and ...
Leaves — Colour, Shape, Texture and Veins
Leaves of different plants differ in colour, shape, texture and smell, and have lines called veins arranged in different ways — ...
Web of Life
All living beings — and natural things like the Sun and water — are connected

items: On a nature trail we explore plants and animals in their home; a nature scientist guides us, and we follow safety rules so that we stay safe and do not harm nature.
A nature scientist studies plants and animals.
Safety rules keep us safe and keep nature unharmed.
Watch and enjoy — do not tease, feed, damage or litter.
Many animals live on land in the forest. Each has its own feature — like the elephant's long trunk — and we can tell animals apart by their features and even by their footprints.
Each animal has its own special feature.
Animals that look alike can be told apart by features.
Footprints tell us which animals visited a place.
Birds differ in colour, eyesight, beaks and claws. The shape of a bird's beak and claws matches the food it eats, so by looking at them we can guess its eating habits.
Birds have different beaks, claws and food habits.
Beak shape + claws = clue to what a bird eats.
Owls see well at night; peacocks are colourful.
Animals that live in and around water move in different ways and have special features to survive there — fins, webbed feet, shells and long snouts; frogs can live both on land and in water.
Fins → swim; webbed feet → swim easily; shell → safety; long thin snout → catch fish.
Frogs live on land and in water.
Insects are tiny animals with three pairs of legs and one pair of antennae to sense their surroundings; some, like flies and grasshoppers, also have two pairs of wings.
Insect = 3 pairs of legs + 1 pair of antennae.
Antennae sense the surroundings.
Some insects have 2 pairs of wings.

notes.h: Leaves — Colour, Shape, Texture and Veins
items: Leaves of different plants differ in colour, shape, texture and smell, and have lines called veins arranged in different ways — so a leaf helps us identify its plant.
Leaves differ in colour, shape, texture and smell.
Lines on leaves are veins.
Veins are arranged in different ways.
All living beings — and natural things like the Sun and water — are connected. Plants and animals depend on each other, and if one part of the web disappears, the whole web weakens.
Everything in nature is connected.
Plants and animals depend on each other.
Remove one part → the web weakens.
Wrong: Feeding a monkey or a bird in the forest is kind and helps it. Right: Our food can make animals sick and change their habits — the rule is: do not feed animals
Wrong: All squirrels look the same. Right: The Indian Giant Squirrel is big and red — very different from the small striped squirrel near our homes
Wrong: All birds eat the same food, like grains. Right: Different birds eat seeds, fruits, nectar, fish or small animals — their beaks show which
Wrong: All water animals swim. Right: A crab walks and a frog jumps; animals in and around water move in different ways
Wrong: A spider is an insect. Right: A spider has four pairs (8) legs and no antennae, so it is not an insect (added)
Wrong: All leaves are the same — just green. Right: Leaves differ in colour, shape, texture and smell

sol_items: Rules to follow in a zoo or forest; why important?: Do not feed or tease animals, do not litter, do not bring pets, firearms or polythene bags. They keep us and nature safe.
Identify the animals in the forest picture: land animal...: Land: elephant, deer, squirrel. Birds: hornbill, peacock, owl. Read from the picture.
Name animals and birds you have seen with one feat: Elephant: long trunk. Peacock: colourful feathers.
Compare the Indian Giant Squirrel with squirrels in you...: The giant squirrel is big and red; the common squirrel is small and striped.
Guess from footprints which animals came to the pond; d...: Match each print with its animal. Draw a print of any animal.
Name the birds shown: Match each picture with its name.
imp_items: Who is a nature scientist?
A person who studies plants and animals
Why should we not tease animals in a forest?
They get scared or angry and may attack
Name two things we should not bring to a forest.
Pets and polythene bags
What does an elephant use its trunk for?
To take food and water
How can footprints help us?
They tell us which animals visited a place
Why does a sunbird have a long beak?
To drink nectar from flowers

topics: Houses Made from Nature
Village houses are built from natural materials found nearby — clay, hay and cow dung — so they are cheap and kind to nature
Colours from Nature
Colours can be made from nature — flowers, leaves, bark, roots, rice flour and coloured stones — and used to paint walls, cloth ...
Storing Grains the Natural Way
Villagers keep stored grains safe from insects and pests with natural containers — earthen pots lined with neem leaves and bamboo ...
Plants That Keep Us Healthy
Plants help keep us healthy — neem oil keeps mosquitoes away, tulsi leaves and ajwain seeds help when we are unwell — and a ...
Energy from the Sun
The Sun is a gift of nature: solar panels turn sunlight into electricity that runs bulbs and fans — Reena's village became fully ...
How We Respect Nature
People respect nature: they thank mother nature in festivals, worship plants and animals in rituals, protect sacred groves and ...
Caring for Nature
Nature gives us a lot, but overusing it causes problems — forests deplete; we care for plants and animals by simple actions at ...

items: Village houses are built from natural materials found nearby — clay, hay and cow dung — so they are cheap and kind to nature.
Clay, hay and cow dung are natural materials
Village houses are made from natural materials found nearby
Colours can be made from nature — flowers, leaves, bark, roots, rice flour and coloured stones — and used to paint walls, cloth and Gond art.
Villagers keep stored grains safe from insects and pests with natural containers — earthen pots lined with neem leaves and bamboo baskets coated with cow dung.
Neem leaves inside the pot keep insects away (their strong bitter smell is disliked by insects — added)
The cow-dung coat on the outside of the basket closes its gaps and protects the grain (added: how it works)
Plants help keep us healthy — neem oil keeps mosquitoes away, tulsi leaves and ajwain seeds help when we are unwell — and a first-aid box keeps help ready.
The Sun is a gift of nature: solar panels turn sunlight into electricity that runs bulbs and fans — Reena's village became fully solar-powered.
People respect nature: they thank mother nature in festivals, worship plants and animals in rituals, protect sacred groves and even apologise to bees.
We worship many plants and animals in different parts of our country — a rich tradition of respecting and protecting nature.
Nature gives us a lot, but overusing it causes problems — forests deplete; we care for plants and animals by simple actions at home, school, parks and our locality.
Reena and Amit wondered how they could thank nature — caring for it is our way of saying thank you
Wrong: A house can only be made with things bought from a shop. Right: Village houses are made of clay, hay and cow dung taken from nature
Wrong: All colours come from shops and factories. Right: Colours can be made from flowers, leaves, roots, bark, rice flour and coloured stones
Wrong: Without chemical sprays, stored grains will surely be eaten by insects. Right: Neem leaves in earthen pots and cow-dung-coated baskets keep insects and pests away naturally
Wrong: A home plant remedy can cure every illness, so we never need a doctor. Right: Plant remedies help in small problems; serious injuries and illnesses need a doctor
Wrong: Solar panels make electricity at night too. Right: They need sunlight; at night they make none (stored electricity is used)
Wrong: Festivals are only for fun and have nothing to do with nature. Right: In the harvest festival people pray to mother nature; many rituals honour plants and animals

sol_items: Plants, part used and uses: Tulsi: leaves for cough; ajwain: seeds for stomach ache; neem: oil keeps mosquitoes away.
What should be kept in a first-aid box? Why is first ai...: Bandage, cotton, antiseptic, plaster and scissors. First aid gives quick help before a doctor comes.
Imagine no electricity for two days: No light, fans or fridge; we use candles and hand fans and live more simply.
What things do we use from nature in daily life?: Food: grains and fruits. Clothing: cotton. Healthcare: neem and tulsi. Other: wood and water.
Challenges when we overuse natural resources: Forests deplete and water, soil and fish become less.
How can we protect the natural environment at home, sch...: Save water, plant trees, avoid plastic and keep surroundings clean.
imp_items: Name three natural materials used for village houses.
Clay, hay and cow dung
Why are village houses made of natural materials cheap and kind to nature?
They are found nearby and return to the soil
Name three natural sources of colour.
Flowers, leaves and bark
How do neem leaves help in storing grains?
Insects dislike their smell, so grains stay safe
How does a cow-dung coat protect a bamboo basket?
It closes the gaps and keeps pests out
Name two plants and their uses.
Tulsi leaves for cough; ajwain seeds for stomach ache

title: Food for Health
intro: In Class 4 EVS Chapter 5, Food for Health, the topics are: Six Tastes of Food (Shad Rasa), food groups, a balanced food plate, water for health, say ‘no’ to junk food, different methods of cooking. topics: Six Tastes of Food (Shad Rasa)
Food can have six tastes — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent (shad rasa)
Food Groups
No single food contains all the nutrients our body needs, so we eat a variety
A Balanced Food Plate
A balanced plate has food in the right quantities from all three food groups — protective foods the most, then body-building ...
Water for Health
Water is an important part of our diet: it helps digest food, keeps our skin and body healthy and removes waste through urine, ...
Say ‘No’ to Junk Food
Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar and is not healthy if eaten regularly and in large quantities; fresh ...
Different Methods of Cooking
Food is cooked by boiling, steaming, frying, roasting, grilling and baking; some foods like fruit chaat and salads are eaten ...

items: Food can have six tastes — sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent (shad rasa). One dish can blend many tastes, and Ayurveda says balanced food with shad rasa is good for health.
Six tastes: sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter, astringent
In Ayurveda the six tastes are called shad rasa
Blended in the right measure, tastes make food more enjoyable
No single food contains all the nutrients our body needs, so we eat a variety. Foods are grouped by their job: energy-giving, body-building and protective.
Food is required for balanced growth of our body
Our body needs a variety of food to stay healthy, energetic and strong
No single food contains all the nutrients — eat a variety
Three food groups: energy-giving, body-building, protective
A balanced plate has food in the right quantities from all three food groups — protective foods the most, then body-building foods, and some energy-giving foods.
All three food groups on one plate
Protective most → body-building → some energy-giving
A balanced plate keeps us healthy, active and happy
Water is an important part of our diet: it helps digest food, keeps our skin and body healthy and removes waste through urine, sweat and faeces.
Water is part of our diet
Digests food · keeps skin healthy · removes waste
Water-rich fruits also give water
Junk food has high amounts of oil, salt and sugar and is not healthy if eaten regularly and in large quantities; fresh home-cooked food is better, and labels on packed food must be checked.
Junk food: high oil, salt, sugar
Unhealthy if eaten regularly and in large quantities
Fresh home-cooked food is better; check labels
Food is cooked by boiling, steaming, frying, roasting, grilling and baking; some foods like fruit chaat and salads are eaten without cooking; a solar cooker cooks with sunlight.
Six methods: boiling, steaming, frying, roasting, grilling, baking
Some foods are eaten raw: fruit chaat, salads
Solar cooker: sunlight, no smoke or ash
Wrong: Pungent means sour. Right: Pungent (teekha) is the hot, spicy taste of green chilli; sour (khatta) is the taste of tamarind
Wrong: Only fruits and vegetables are healthy food. Right: We need all three groups: energy-giving, body-building and protective
Wrong: A balanced plate has equal amounts of every food. Right: Protective foods are the most, then body-building, then some energy-giving foods
Wrong: Water is not food, so it is not part of our diet. Right: The book says water is an important part of our diet
Wrong: Junk food means any food that tastes good. Right: Junk food has high oil, salt and sugar; tasty home-cooked food is not junk
Wrong: All food must be cooked before eating. Right: Fruit chaat and vegetable salads are eaten without cooking

sol_items: Identify food items having at least three tastes: Chaat has sweet, sour, salty and spicy tastes.
Why do we need different kinds of food?: No single food has all the nutrients.
What if we eat from a single food group every day?: The body misses the jobs of the other groups, so we do not grow well and fall ill more easily.
Food diary: circle healthy items, X unhealthy ones, fin...: Add fruits or pulses if a group is missing.
Do you help in cooking at home? Should all family membe...: Yes, everyone should so that the work is shared.
Food collage: energy-giving, body-building and protecti...: Energy: rice, potato. Body-building: dal, peanuts. Protective: fruits and vegetables.
imp_items: Name the six tastes.
Sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent
What is shad rasa?
The six tastes in Ayurveda
Which taste is green chilli?
Pungent
Why do we need different kinds of food?
No single food has all the nutrients
Give two examples of each food group.
Energy: rice, potato. Body-building: dal, peanuts. Protective: spinach, orange
What happens if we eat from one food group only?
The body misses the jobs of other groups

subject: EVS
title: Happy and Healthy Living
intro: In Class 4 EVS Chapter 6, Happy and Healthy Living, the topics are: Journey of the Grains, thank you everyone! — gratitude for food, mindful eating, valuing food, enjoy sports — exercise, games and yoga, sleep well too!, feeling safe — safe and unsafe touch. Read the short notes, check every book question with the NCERT solutions, practise the important questions and then try the 30-mark sample paper. All four PDFs are free to download.
topics: Journey of the Grains
The food we enjoy is made from grains, pulses and vegetables
Thank You Everyone! — Gratitude for Food
When we remember everyone who helped bring our food with love and gratitude, we feel the importance of each grain and enjoy its ...
Mindful Eating
Mindful eating means paying attention to what we eat and how we feel while eating — eating slowly, chewing well and enjoying ...
Valuing Food
Every grain is precious
Enjoy Sports — Exercise, Games and Yoga
Along with good food we need regular exercise
Sleep Well too!
Our body needs enough sleep every day
Feeling Safe — Safe and Unsafe Touch
Sometimes someone may feel unhappy, unsafe or uncomfortable

items: The food we enjoy is made from grains, pulses and vegetables. A grain makes a long journey from the farm to our plate, made possible by soil, water, sunlight, animals and the hard work of many people.
Food items are made from grains, pulses and vegetables.
The journey of the grain from the farm to our plate is long and needs elements, animals and people.

notes.h: Thank You Everyone! — Gratitude for Food
items: When we remember everyone who helped bring our food with love and gratitude, we feel the importance of each grain and enjoy its taste. Many Indian festivals thank Mother Nature for food.
When we remember all the contributors with love and gratitude, we feel the importance of each grain.
Gratitude also makes us enjoy the taste of food.
Mindful eating means paying attention to what we eat and how we feel while eating — eating slowly, chewing well and enjoying every bite.
Every grain is precious. When we waste food, we fail to respect the hard work of everyone who brought it to our plate.
Every grain is precious.
Wasting food means not respecting the hard work of farmers, sellers, cooks and everyone else.

notes.h: Enjoy Sports — Exercise, Games and Yoga
items: Along with good food we need regular exercise. Playing outdoors, running, jumping, cycling and skipping keep us strong and energetic; yoga improves our posture and keeps us happy and active.
Regular physical activities keep us strong and energetic.
Yoga improves our posture and keeps us happy and active.
'Khel Yoga', the Physical Education and Well-being textbook, has many more exercises and games.
Our body needs enough sleep every day. Good sleep takes away tiredness and makes us fresh; without it we feel tired, sleepy, irritable and cannot focus.
Our body requires sufficient sleep every day.
Getting enough sleep is just as important as eating healthy and exercising.

notes.h: Feeling Safe — Safe and Unsafe Touch
items: Sometimes someone may feel unhappy, unsafe or uncomfortable. A safe touch makes us happy and comfortable; an unsafe touch makes us uneasy, scared or confused. If we feel unsafe, we say 'No' and tell a trusted adult.
Wrong: Food comes from the shop. Right: The shop is only one stop; the grain grows on a farm and travels a long way to reach the shop and our plate
Wrong: We need to thank only the cook who served the food. Right: We thank everyone on the journey — farmer, cattle, shopkeeper, cook, family — and nature: soil, water and sun
Wrong: Eating fast while watching TV is fine — food is just to fill the stomach. Right: When we eat slowly and pay attention, we enjoy food more and make healthier choices
Wrong: Leaving a little food on the plate does not matter. Right: Every grain is precious — even a little waste disrespects the work of many people
Wrong: Watching a cricket match on TV is a physical activity. Right: Physical activity means moving our own body — running, jumping, cycling, skipping, yoga
Wrong: Sleep is a waste of time — more play time is better. Right: Sleep is as important as food and exercise; it takes away tiredness and makes us fresh

sol_items: Connect the food items with the ingredients used to mak...: Roti: wheat. Idli: rice and urad dal. Chips: potato.
Tick the elements that help a grain in its journey: Soil, air, water, farmer, earthworm, insect.
Role of farmers; roles of soil, water, cattle, shopkeep...: Farmer grows the grain; soil and water feed it; cattle help the farmer; shopkeeper sells it; family cooks it.
Role of your tongue in mindful eating; what teeth do; w...: The tongue tastes and moves food; teeth break it into small soft pieces; saliva makes it soft and easy to swallow.
What if someone offers you more food than you need? A f...: Politely say no and take a small portion; try a little and leave nothing wasted.
Activities people do in the park picture; which physica...: Running, skipping, cycling and yoga. After play I feel happy and tired.
imp_items: What would happen to a grain if there were no water?
The plant would dry up and no grain would grow
Name four helpers in the journey of a grain.
Soil, water, farmer and shopkeeper
What is gratitude?
Remembering with love and thanks all who helped us
Name two festivals that thank Mother Nature for food.
Makar Sankranti and Onam
What is mindful eating?
Paying attention to what we eat and how we feel
Why should we chew food well?
Teeth break it into small soft pieces and we enjoy the taste

topics: Which Objects Spin?
Some objects, like a coin, a bangle and a top, spin well; others, like an eraser, do not spin properly

A cardboard spinner with the toothpick (hole) at the centre is the same from all sides, so it stays upright and spins; with the ...

items: Some objects, like a coin, a bangle and a top, spin well; others, like an eraser, do not spin properly. A spinning object slows down, shakes and then stops.
Coins, bangles and tops spin; erasers do not spin properly.
A spinning coin slows down and shakes before it stops.
Fans, potter's wheels, the charkha and the lattu all spin.

notes.h: Making a Spinner That Spins Well
items: A cardboard spinner with the toothpick (hole) at the centre is the same from all sides, so it stays upright and spins; with the hole away from the centre it does not spin properly. Shape and colours can also be changed.
Hole at the centre → same from all sides → upright and spins.
Hole away from the centre → not the same from all sides → does not spin well (maybe the side with more card is heavier — added).
A spinning square looks circular.
Balance means the same weight on all sides of the centre.
Many heavy things (iron nail) sink and many light things (leaf) float — but floating or sinking cannot be decided only by heavy or light; it also depends on other factors.
Guess first, then drop and check.
Many heavy things sink and light things float — but not all.
Heavy or light is not the only factor.
The same aluminium foil floats when spread out or made into a cup, and sinks when pressed into a tight ball — by changing the shape we can make an object float or sink.
Same foil, different shape, different result.
Spread out or cup → floats; tight ball → sinks.
Press the ball tightly — trapped air can make it float.
A good boat must float and keep its balance. Boats made of different materials have different strengths and challenges — some break easily, some tip over — and we can improve them.
A boat must float AND balance.
Every boat has strengths and challenges.
Compare, then improve the design.
Wrong: All objects can spin well. Right: Some objects, like an eraser, do not spin properly
Wrong: The toothpick can go anywhere in the card. Right: At the centre it spins; away from the centre it does not spin properly
Wrong: Heavy things always sink and light things always float. Right: Floating or sinking cannot be decided just by heavy or light — a heavy steel bowl or pumpkin floats, a light pin sinks
Wrong: The same thing will always float or always sink — shape does not matter. Right: The same foil floats as a cup and sinks as a tight ball
Wrong: Any boat that floats is a good boat. Right: It must also stay strong and keep its balance without tipping over

sol_items: Do all objects spin? List objects that can spin: No. Coin, bangle, top, fan and potters wheel spin; an eraser does not spin properly.
Make four spinners; record whether each spins: The spinner with the hole at the centre spins well.
Which spinners did not spin properly? Reasons? Did the ...: The ones with the hole away from the centre; the card is not the same from all sides. Yes, the position mattered.
Other card shapes as spinners; colour spinners in diffe...: A square looks like a circle when it spins. Colours mix and look different.
What other things have you seen spinning?: Ceiling fan, charkha, lattu, potters wheel.
Guess float or sink for leaf, nail, bowl, stone, bottle...: Leaf floats; nail and stone sink; an empty bowl floats; a closed empty bottle floats.
imp_items: What does spin mean?
To turn round and round quickly on one point
Name two things at home that spin.
Ceiling fan and top
What does a spinning coin do as it slows down?
It shakes and then stops
Your spinner wobbles and falls. What do you check first?
Whether the toothpick is exactly at the centre
What shape does a spinning square card look like?
A circle
What is float and what is sink?
Float: stay on top of water. Sink: go down to the bottom

topics: Where Paper Comes From
Paper is made from trees
How to Make Recycled Paper
Old paper can be turned into new paper: tear and soak it with fenugreek seeds, mash it into a paste, roll it into thin sheets and ...
Colouring Paper with Natural Dyes
Paper can be coloured with natural dyes made from plant parts, or with artificial dyes
Types of Paper and Their Uses
We use different kinds of paper for different purposes — what a paper is like (thin, soft, thick, hard, bumpy) decides its use
Refuse and Reduce: Making Less Waste
The 5Rs are a 5-step plan to reduce waste

Reuse (use again), Repurpose (use in a new, creative way) and Recycle (a process that makes something new) give old things a new ...

items: Paper is made from trees. Book paper is made from wood pulp, and making it needs many trees, a lot of water and energy — so we must use paper only when needed.
A large number of trees are cut to make paper from wood pulp.
Making paper needs many trees, a lot of water and energy.
Use paper and other materials responsibly — only when needed.
Old paper can be turned into new paper: tear and soak it with fenugreek seeds, mash it into a paste, roll it into thin sheets and let them dry.
Recycling paper saves trees.
Order: collect → pulp → mash → roll out → dry.
Paper can be coloured with natural dyes made from plant parts, or with artificial dyes. Natural dyes are safe and also colour clothes and pots.

notes.h: Types of Paper and Their Uses
items: We use different kinds of paper for different purposes — what a paper is like (thin, soft, thick, hard, bumpy) decides its use.
Property decides use.
Braille paper lets visually challenged people read by touch.

notes.h: Refuse and Reduce: Making Less Waste
items: The 5Rs are a 5-step plan to reduce waste. The first two, Refuse and Reduce, stop waste before it is made.
Refuse = say NO.
Reduce = use LESS, carefully.
Reuse (use again), Repurpose (use in a new, creative way) and Recycle (a process that makes something new) give old things a new life.
Reuse — again.
Repurpose — new use.
Recycle — new thing.
Small changes help the environment, save resources and reduce pollution.
Wrong: Paper is made in factories and has nothing to do with trees. Right: Book paper is made from wood pulp (book); newspaper too comes from trees (book) — from wood pulp (added)
Wrong: Fenugreek seeds are added to give paper colour or smell. Right: They are a binding material — they help the pulp stick together
Wrong: Natural colours come only from flowers. Right: They come from many plant parts — leaf, flower, root, seed and stem
Wrong: All paper is the same, so any paper can do any job. Right: Each kind has its own properties, so it suits a different use
Wrong: Refuse means throwing things away. Right: Refuse means saying no to taking things that make waste at all
Wrong: Reuse and repurpose mean the same thing. Right: Reuse = same job again; repurpose = a new, creative job

sol_items: How are trees and paper related to each other?: Paper is made from wood pulp, which comes from trees.
Make recycled paper from old newspapers, fenugreek seed...: Tear and soak the paper with methi, mash it into a paste, roll it into sheets and dry them.
Colour same-size pieces with turmeric, spinach, beetroo...: Turmeric: yellow; spinach: green; beetroot: pink; henna: brown. Record which is brightest.
Make a greeting card or mask from recycled paper: Cut, decorate with natural colours and display.
Do we waste paper? How can we reduce wastage?: Yes. Use both sides, reuse blank pages and avoid tearing out pages.
Paste different kinds of paper and write their use: Newspaper for reading; thick card for covers; tissue paper for wrapping; Braille paper for reading by touch.
imp_items: What is wood pulp?
Wood broken and mashed into a soft wet mass
Why must we use paper only when needed?
Making paper needs many trees, a lot of water and energy
Name two things people wrote on before paper.
Cloth and palm leaves
What is recycled paper?
New paper made from old used paper
Why are fenugreek seeds added?
They bind the pulp so it sticks together
What are natural dyes? Give two sources.
Colours from plant parts; turmeric and beetroot

title: Different Lands, Different Lives
intro: In Class 4 EVS Chapter 9, Different Lands, Different Lives, the topics are: Kinds of Landforms — Four Holidays, Four Lands, plains — the land of agriculture, desert — the land of endless sand, coastal region — life by the sea, mountains — life in the cold heights, living with challenges — cyclones, landslides, little water, life in each landform — four landforms compared. topics: Kinds of Landforms — Four Holidays, Four Lands
Land is not the same everywhere
Plains — the Land of Agriculture
Plains are flat lands with large fields and rich, fertile soil, so many people are farmers and their food comes from their crops
Desert — the Land of Endless Sand
A desert is a dry place with very little rainfall
Coastal Region — Life by the Sea
A coastal region is land next to the sea
Mountains — Life in the Cold Heights
Mountains are rocky landforms that rise high above the ground and are usually cold
Living with Challenges — Cyclones, Landslides, Little Water
Each landform brings its own difficulty: little water in the desert, cyclones on the coast, landslides in the mountains
Life in Each Landform — Four Landforms Compared
The kind of land decides the trees, animals, houses, clothes, food, work, festivals and art of the people living there

notes.h: Kinds of Landforms — Four Holidays, Four Lands
items: Land is not the same everywhere. Plains, deserts, coastal regions and mountains are different kinds of land (landforms), and people in each live differently.
Four kinds of landforms: plains, desert, coastal region, mountains
Each kind of land has its own plants, animals, food, clothes and houses
Plains are flat lands with large fields and rich, fertile soil, so many people are farmers and their food comes from their crops.
Plains: flat, large fields, fertile soil
Many people are farmers
Food: makki di roti, sarson da saag, lassi

notes.h: Desert — the Land of Endless Sand
items: A desert is a dry place with very little rainfall. Its plants and animals can live on very little water, and people's houses, clothes and food suit the dry land.
Desert = dry, very little rainfall
Plants: cactus, khejri, babool
Camel = ship of the desert
Tankas store water

notes.h: Coastal Region — Life by the Sea
items: A coastal region is land next to the sea. Many people there depend on fishing, the beaches give shells and sand, and the sea is home to many creatures.
Coastal region = land by the sea
Fishing is the main livelihood of many
Puri: sand art, shells, Jagannath Temple, Rath Yatra

notes.h: Mountains — Life in the Cold Heights
items: Mountains are rocky landforms that rise high above the ground and are usually cold. People's clothes, houses, food, animals and trees suit the cold.
Mountains: rocky, high, cold, steep slopes, valleys
Yak for travel; oak, pine, walnut, chestnut
Thukpa, sel roti; Loosong and Namsoong

notes.h: Living with Challenges — Cyclones, Landslides, Little Water
items: Each landform brings its own difficulty: little water in the desert, cyclones on the coast, landslides in the mountains. Warnings, preparation and helping each other keep people safe.
Desert — little water; coast — cyclones; mountains — landslides
Warnings + preparation + community help = safety

notes.h: Life in Each Landform — Four Landforms Compared
items: The kind of land decides the trees, animals, houses, clothes, food, work, festivals and art of the people living there.
Land → plants and animals → food, clothes, houses, work, festivals
Every landform has gifts and challenges
Wrong: Land is the same everywhere. Right: Some land is flat, some sandy and dry, some by the sea and some high and rocky
Wrong: Makki di roti is made from wheat flour. Right: It is made with corn (makki) flour
Wrong: Nothing grows in a desert. Right: Cactus, khejri and babool grow there — they survive on very little water
Wrong: People on the coast live mainly by farming like in the plains. Right: Many coastal people depend on fishing
Wrong: Mountains are warm because they are closer to the Sun. Right: Mountains are usually cold; high peaks are covered in snow
Wrong: Nothing can be done when a cyclone comes. Right: Early warnings and advance preparation save many lives — Odisha won awards for it

sol_items: Plains picture: Flat land with large fields; people farm and harvest; cows and buffaloes; colourful turbans and dupattas.
Why is water scarce in the desert?: Very little rain falls there.
Beach picture: activities; trees near the sea; fun acti...: Fishing, swimming, building sand castles. Palm and coconut trees grow near the sea. Light cotton clothes suit the warm, damp weather.
How does life around the coast differ from life in a de...: The coast has water, fishing and beaches; the desert is dry, with camels and cactus.
Why keep beaches clean?: Waste harms sea creatures and spoils the beach for everyone.
Adverse effects of a cyclone; how can communities : Strong winds and rain damage houses and crops. Early warnings, shelters and helping each other keep people safe.
imp_items: Name the four landforms.
Plains, desert, coastal region and mountains
What is a landform?
A kind of land on the Earths surface
Why do many people in plains do farming?
The land is flat with rich fertile soil
What is makki di roti made from?
Corn flour
What is a desert? Name two desert plants.
A dry place with little rain; cactus and khejri
Why is the camel called the ship of the desert?
It travels over sand carrying people and goods

intro: In Class 4 EVS Chapter 10, Our Sky, the topics are: The Sky Changes Through the Day, the sun and its journey across the sky, how a shadow changes, shadows through the day, stars and the shapes of the moon, moon calendars, moon festivals and chandrayaan. topics: The Sky Changes Through the Day
The sky does not look the same all day: its colour and the Sun's colour change from morning to afternoon to night, and birds, ...
The Sun and Its Journey Across the Sky
The Sun is the brightest object in the sky and gives us light and heat
How a Shadow Changes
A shadow forms when an object blocks light
Shadows Through the Day
Shadows made by the Sun are long in the morning, short at noon and long again in the evening, pointing the opposite way — because ...
Stars and the Shapes of the Moon
After sunset the sky fills with twinkling stars in patterns
Moon Calendars, Moon Festivals and Chandrayaan
Because the Moon's shapes come back regularly, ancient people used them to count days — the earliest calendars — and many ...

notes.h: The Sky Changes Through the Day
items: The sky does not look the same all day: its colour and the Sun's colour change from morning to afternoon to night, and birds, animals, plants and people change what they do.
The colour of the sky changes in the morning, afternoon and at night.
The Sun's colour also appears to change.
The size and shape of the Moon seem to change over time.
Birds, animals, trees and humans do different things at different times of the day.

notes.h: The Sun and Its Journey Across the Sky
items: The Sun is the brightest object in the sky and gives us light and heat. Every day it appears to rise in the East, come overhead at noon and set in the West.
The Sun appears to move from the East to overhead till noon, then gradually towards the West.
We say 'appears to move' — this is the visible journey of the Sun.
A shadow forms when an object blocks light. Bring the object closer to the light and the shadow gets bigger; change the direction of the light and the shadow points another way.
Shadows are not only made in sunlight — a torch also makes them.
Every object that blocks light makes a shadow.

Shadows made by the Sun are long in the morning, short at noon and long again in the evening, pointing the opposite way — because the Sun appears to move from East to overhead to West. People used this to tell time with a sundial.
Morning shadows are long, noon shadows are short, evening shadows are long again.
Evening shadows point the opposite way to morning shadows.
The shadow's direction changes because the Sun appears to move from East to West.

notes.h: Stars and the Shapes of the Moon
items: After sunset the sky fills with twinkling stars in patterns. The Moon looks like the biggest object at night, and its shape changes night after night — from a full circle (Poornima) to no Moon at all (Amavasya) — again and again.
The shape of the Moon looks different on different nights.
Full Moon = Poornima (complete circle); New Moon = Amavasya (not visible).
The shapes come back again and again — periodically.

notes.h: Moon Calendars, Moon Festivals and Chandrayaan
items: Because the Moon's shapes come back regularly, ancient people used them to count days — the earliest calendars — and many festivals are fixed by the Moon. Today India has even landed on the Moon with Chandrayaan.
The Moon's shapes repeat, so people could count days with them.
Many festivals are fixed by the Moon's shape.
Wrong: The sky looks the same all day. Right: Its colour changes — orange in the morning, bright in the afternoon, dark at night
Wrong: There are no stars in the sky during the day. Right: Stars are there, but the Sun is so bright that we cannot see them
Wrong: Shadows are formed only in sunlight. Right: Any light makes shadows — a torch, a bulb, a lamp
Wrong: The evening shadow points the same way as the morning shadow. Right: It points the opposite way, because the Sun is now on the other (West) side
Wrong: The Moon is always round. Right: It is a complete circle only on Poornima; on other nights it looks like a C, a half, or is not seen
Wrong: Diwali is celebrated on a full-Moon night. Right: Diwali is on the night when there is no Moon in the sky

sol_items: Draw the sky in the morning, afternoon and at night; wr...: Morning: orange sky and Sun. Afternoon: bright blue sky. Night: dark sky with the Moon and stars.
Compare observations; changes in animals and plants; th...: Birds fly out in the morning and return in the evening; flowers close at night. The brightest object is the Sun.
When the Sun rises and sets: sky, birds and animals, ch...: Rise: orange sky, birds sing, we wake up. Set: sky turns red, birds return to nests, lights come on at home.
Differences in the morning, noon and evening shado: Long in the morning, short at noon, long again in the evening and pointing the opposite way.
How does my shadow change? Why? Does this happen to all...: The Sun appears to move, so the shadow changes. It happens to all objects. Any light makes shadows, such as a torch.
Change the distance of the light source from the stick;...: Closer to the light makes the shadow bigger; changing the torch direction turns the shadow the other way.
imp_items: Which is the brightest object in the sky?
The Sun
Give two differences between day and night.
Day is bright with the Sun; night is dark with the Moon and stars
What colour is the sky at sunrise?
Orange
In which direction does the Sun rise and set?
Rises in the East and sets in the West
Why can we not see stars in the day?
The Sun is so bright that we cannot see them
What is a shadow?
The dark shape formed behind an object that blocks light
